evidence: The trusted staging worktree's VerificationCommandPolicy has argv/required/timeoutMs but no cwd.
forge_verify always executes approved commands at the worktree root, so npm scripts cannot target a package directory.
forge:init copies a template that blindly selects root npm test and does not inspect package manifests.

<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

### Verdict/Confidence/Severity/Task Type

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Confirmed |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | High |
| Task type | Bug fix |

### What Was Claimed

A structurally valid required verification policy can pass setup and launch repository writers even when its command is impossible at the repository root in a monorepo. The approved command set cannot express the package directory where the command is valid, and the failure is discovered only after implementation.

### What We Found

- `src/core/policy.ts` validates `argv`, `required`, and `timeoutMs`, but has no validated command working directory.
- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` binds those three fields and `forge_verify` executes every command with the worktree root as its cwd.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` loads policy and prepares a worktree before any repository-aware verification preflight; the writer is launched through `spawnWorkOn` without checking required command executability, cwd, or npm scripts.
- `src/ui/commands.ts` and `templates/config.json` select root `npm test` without inspecting package manifests.

### Root Cause

Verification policy is treated as an argv-only execution contract. There is no safe, read-only semantic preflight of the configured command against the repository layout, and the child runtime has no package-scoped cwd to honor.

### Affected Files

- `src/core/policy.ts` — add a normalized, repository-relative command cwd.
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` — add non-executing cwd, executable, and npm-script validation.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` — run required-command preflight before launching the writer.
- `src/adapters/subagents.ts` and `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` — bind, validate, and execute commands from the approved cwd.
- `src/ui/commands.ts` and `templates/config.json` — make init repository-aware and emit safe cwd values.
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts`, `test/core/policy.test.ts`, and related fixtures — cover monorepo and fail-closed regressions.

### Evidence

- The frozen policy interface and parser contain no `cwd` field.
- `forge_verify` passes the assigned worktree root directly to the process runner.
- `forge:init` copies a template whose required command is root `npm test` and never reads package scripts.
- The work-on start path calls `git.prepare` and then `spawnWorkOn` without a verification preflight.

### History Findings

The issue's described failure mode is consistent with the current staging-base implementation. The trusted parent separately validated setup from installed main; the staging worktree intentionally does not contain `.forge/config.json`, so no policy file is to be copied into the implementation diff. No prior run for issue #94 was present before this bound run.

### Recommendation

Add a portable relative `cwd` to each tracked verification command, validate it without executing repository code, inspect package.json only to verify npm script existence, preflight all required local commands before writer launch, and run approved checks from the bound cwd while preserving required-check failure semantics.

### Related Issues

- None required for this bounded fix.

### Decomposition Assessment

The change is standard complexity, cohesive across the policy/preflight/binding/runtime/init surfaces, and does not require decomposition or a product decision.

### Acceptance Spec

- Required commands fail before writer launch when their executable, cwd, or npm script is unavailable.
- Errors identify the exact `verification.commands.<name>` config path and provide `/forge:init` or config remediation.
- A monorepo package cwd is accepted and used by `forge_verify`.
- `/forge:init` does not generate an impossible root npm test command.
- A genuinely failing approved command remains a required verification failure.
- Regression tests cover a root without a test script and a package with one.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

evidence: The contract keeps all verification policy and runtime changes inside the assigned worktree and excludes .forge/config.json.
The implementation will preserve argv-only execution and required-check fail-closed semantics while adding a relative cwd and read-only preflight.
The init path will choose a package-scoped npm test only when a discovered package manifest defines scripts.test; otherwise it will emit an empty local-command set for explicit CI-only verification.

## Builder Contract

### Objective

Prevent impossible required local verification policies from launching repository writers, while allowing safe package-scoped commands in monorepos and preserving fail-closed verification after implementation.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/core/policy.ts`
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts`
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`
- `src/adapters/subagents.ts`
- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts`
- `src/ui/commands.ts`
- `templates/config.json`
- `test/core/policy.test.ts`
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts`
- `test/ui/commands.test.ts`
- `test/fixtures/verification-monorepo/**`

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not add or copy `.forge/config.json` into the staging worktree.
- Do not alter protected-branch, lease, merge, GitHub authority, or review policy outside the verification contract.
- Do not execute repository scripts during preflight.
- Do not weaken required-check failure handling or allow arbitrary shell strings.
- Do not add dependencies or change unrelated product behavior.

### Invariants

- Verification commands remain trusted argv arrays and are executed only by bound command name.
- Every command cwd is normalized as a repository-relative path and cannot escape the repository.
- Required command preflight completes before any writer child is launched.
- Missing executable, package directory, or npm script fails with the exact config path and actionable remediation.
- Empty local verification commands are valid only as explicit CI-only verification; required post-implementation failures still block.

### Deliverables

1. Validated command cwd support with backward-compatible root default.
2. Read-only repository verification preflight and monorepo regression coverage.
3. Repository-aware `/forge:init` command selection with CI-only fallback.
4. Bound child execution from the approved cwd.
5. Typecheck/test evidence and a clean implementation commit.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| cwd field | Normalize `verification.commands.<name>.cwd` in policy and carry it through template/binding/runtime. |
| safe init | Inspect package.json manifests without executing scripts; select matching package cwd or emit CI-only commands. |
| preflight before writers | Invoke `preflightVerificationCommands` from work-on start before `spawnWorkOn`. |
| actionable failure | Include `verification.commands.<name>` config path plus `/forge:init` or cwd/config remediation in thrown errors. |
| monorepo regression | Add a root-without-test and package-with-test fixture/test. |
| fail closed | Keep required command result mapping/status unchanged and test required failures remain blocking. |

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### History

The frozen staging base predates the monorepo verification fix. The trusted parent validated setup from installed main; the staging worktree intentionally lacks `.forge/config.json`, which remains excluded from the patch.

### Callers and Data Flow

`ForgeWorkOnController.startIssue` loads policy and prepares the run; `SubagentsRpcClient.spawnWorkOn` serializes verification policy into the child binding; `forge_verify` resolves a bound command and runs it; `verificationForGate` converts child results into merge-gate evidence.

### CI Surface

The repository uses strict TypeScript and Node test discovery via `npm run check`. Local verification may be empty when CI owns checks; the work-on child must not invent an unapproved command.

### Prior Findings

The investigation confirmed argv-only policy, root-only execution, blind template selection, and no pre-writer semantic preflight.

### Hazards

Package manifest parsing must remain data-only. Cwd normalization must reject absolute paths, parent traversal, backslashes, NULs, missing directories, and symlink escapes. Runtime binding must independently validate cwd rather than trusting model output.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Extend policy parsing with normalized repository-relative `cwd`, permit an empty command map for explicit CI-only verification, and update template/tests.
2. Add `verification-preflight.ts` to validate required command cwd directories, executable availability, and npm script presence by reading package.json only; surface config-path remediation.
3. Invoke preflight from `startIssue` before worktree/writer launch and retain the trusted policy path in errors.
4. Propagate cwd through subagent bindings and child runtime; execute `forge_verify` from the approved package cwd while preserving status/exit-code semantics.
5. Update `/forge:init` to inspect package manifests and choose a valid package-scoped test command or explicit CI-only configuration; add fixture/tests.
6. Run diagnostics and the named repository check, inspect the diff, commit implementation, and continue through review.

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
